title: Natty or not (.com): Alpha Destiny
summary: NH dissects a natty-or-not article accusing Alpha Destiny of steroid use, agreeing only with its description of naturals' hope-and-despair cycle. He attacks its body fat estimates, FFMI reliance, strawman arguments and natural-limit claims, and argues that natural training raises the hormonal profile so growth slows but never stops. Along the way he shares his own health reasons for staying natural and views on frame, height and Zyzz.
claims: Many naturals fall into a cycle of hope and despair, jumping to each new method, diet or fad and quitting when it doesn't make them big within months
Inspiration is good but adoration isn't; emulation is good but imitation is bad; stay your own person
Methods sold as revolutionary on YouTube are usually decades old or marketing; people respond to novelty, so 'squat for big quads' gets ignored
No food will make you big; once you hit your macros with healthy foods, it is just a calorie calculation to feed the gains
He has followed Alpha Destiny since 2015 and learned the weighted trap stretch and Olympic rings work from him, though Alex sometimes runs with ideas that are factually wrong
Looking enhanced while natural should be the goal; if after years of training nobody suspects you of using, you have sort of failed
Visible lower abs and serratus depend on muscle size, not just leanness; he shows four serratus and separated obliques at 16-17% body fat
FFMI is a faulty way to judge whether someone is natural, especially with wrong body fat estimates
Wrists and ankles carry essentially no fat, so a full inch of wrist growth from bulking is implausible
Rock climbers like Alex Honnold develop very thick fingers and wrists from tension and possibly callus buildup
His wrists have always been thin and never thickened from training, though the muscles around them grew
A big frame gives potential to carry more mass but doesn't determine whether it is muscle or fat; he has very narrow clavicles yet carries a lot of muscle
His doctor told him he has a genetic predisposition to a disease that exogenous hormones could trigger as early as his early 30s, so PEDs are not an option for him
You cannot predict what a cycle would do to someone because health side effects are unknown and individual
A cycle does not add pure muscle; you gain water and fat too, and you cannot add 20 lb while keeping the same body fat except perhaps as a newbie
Arnold and Serge Nubret were never at 5% body fat; golden-era physiques carried a layer of subcutaneous fat
Frame and height matter on stage: shorter 'giant killers' like Lee Priest never became top dog, and a tall freak with good insertions wins
4000 kcal would make him (6 ft, slow metabolism) gain weight fast, though metabolisms vary
YouTubers routinely exaggerate their calorie intake and understate their body fat
If you have trained hard and eaten properly for years and have no muscle, either you don't train as hard as you think or you have a hormonal issue
Three months of a properly written cycle makes almost anyone look insane; some 19-year-olds on PEDs for life will look better than him effortlessly; steroids work
Nobody can prove natural status; unless paid for tests and time, his word is all there is
Repeated fake-natty deceptions have turned viewers into paranoids or lemmings
He has bad genetics for bodybuilding but looks good because he knows how to train and what to avoid
The natural limit is a topic for losers and beginners; a lifter of five or six years who claims to have hit it just doesn't want to push, which is fine if admitted
Natural-limit talk gives beginners standards set too low, the mirror image of fake-natty unrealistic expectations
No study shows training stops driving hypertrophy; the body is built to survive, so progressively stressing it forces more muscle, slowing over time but never stopping
Short men look bigger faster and on camera through angles; tall men have more potential but it takes longer (e.g. 9 years instead of 3), so they shouldn't compare
Zyzz's physique came from PEDs and height, not his training; he was a terrible role model who spawned an unhealthy aesthetic era
Strength and size correlate only partly; he is weak for his size and many stronger lifters have smaller muscles
Train for your own best physique; picturing a fictional physique as a goal works better than copying someone with different insertions
In naturals, muscle growth and hormonal profile rise together symbiotically; testosterone keeps climbing only as long as you keep pushing training
